To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the surface undergoes a number of structural transformations during CO oxidation.
the Pd(111) surface in CO oxidation at 300 K transforms into a combination (111), (332), and (331) surface structures, while in the presence of large excess of oxygen, a surface oxide is formed.
the Pd(111) surface transforms into the (111) and the (332) surfaces under CO rich conditions and that the (111), (331) and (332) surfaces are present simultaneously under O2 rich conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of step dynamics and oxide formation under changing reaction conditions.
the study of surface structure of Pd(553)-CO and PdO(101)-Pd(553) in a wide range of reaction conditions.
the study of the dynamic behavior of a Pd surface under reaction conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CO oxidation over Pd(553), in a wide range of reaction conditions, is accompanied by a series of structural transformations, which are driven by the adsorbed oxygen atoms.
the surface oxide is formed in the reaction environment only if the reaction is not limited by the availability of oxygen atoms.
the surface structure and the oxide formation are strongly dependent on the reaction conditions, i.e. the excess of CO and O2 over the stoichiometric reaction conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CO oxidation on Pd(553), at least at low pressures, proceeds via a surface oxide formation mechanism.
the PdO layer is not stable under reaction conditions with excess of CO.

the Pd(111) facets are the most stable surface structure under CO rich conditions and that the PdO(101) surface is formed under O2 rich conditions, while the step sites are the most likely place for the formation of an oxygen containing structure under reaction stoichiometry conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface oxide is not formed on the terraces, but on the step edges, and that the oxide is a metastable phase that can be formed only under specific conditions.
the surface structure and the reaction conditions are intimately related, and the reaction conditions can be tuned by changing the reaction environment.
surface oxide structures can be formed on Pd(111) and Pd(331) surfaces, but the presence of steps seems to be crucial for the formation of the oxide structures.
